set_aside.subject: content_identity
set_aside.text: - content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.
set_aside.other_text: - IdentitySubject discriminated union on field 'subject_kind' (exact variants, no others exist): ContractVersionContent (subject_kind='contract_version'), ImplementationContent (subject_kind='implementation'), TrialCaseContent (subject_kind='trial_case'), FlowVersionContent (subject_kind='flow_version'), StoredValueContent (subject_kind='stored_value'), CorpusContent (subject_kind='corpus'), KeyFieldsContent (subject_kind='idempotency_key'), JsonTextContent (subject_kind='json_text'), BytesContent (subject_kind='bytes'); a value of IdentitySubject is an instance of one of these variants, never of another model, and IdentitySubject itself is not constructed
set_aside.question: Must “every content variant of IdentitySubject” be changed to identify only the six listed structured-content variants, or must the parenthetical include all nine union variants despite the separate rules for idempotency_key, json_text, and bytes?
set_aside.set_aside_because: an unchanged passage of a unit reviewed for its change
